Current Research
Uncertainty Quantification for Biomedical Classification
January 2026 - Present | Rutgers University
Advisor: Dr. Gemma Moran

Building probabilistic models to quantify prediction uncertainty in healthcare ML systems
Developing calibration methods that help clinicians understand model confidence, enabling safer deployment of AI in clinical decision support


Interactive R/Shiny App for Clinical Trial Design
June 2025 - Present | Rutgers University
Advisors: Dr. Han Zhang, Dr. Philip He

Built an interactive Shiny application to visualize hypothesis graphs and dynamically redistribute test weights for multiple testing procedures
Extended the open-source trialsimulator R package with node/edge editing and JSON import/export features
The app enables biostatisticians to design and simulate complex multi-arm trials without writing code, reducing trial design time from days to hours

Live Demo: oncotrialdesign.shinyapps.io/graphMTP

Imaging Data Analyst RA - CHOP D3b Center
July 2024 - Present | Philadelphia, PA
Advisor: Dr. Anahita Fathi Kazerooni at the D3b Center

Deployed nnU-Net v2 pipelines on Slurm/GPU clusters for automated pediatric brain tumor segmentation
Implemented Monte Carlo Dropout (20 inference passes/case) to generate uncertainty maps that now support radiologist QA workflows, flagging low-confidence predictions for manual review
Processed 100+ GB of multi-sequence MRI data with automated ETL and quality checks
Contributed to AutoSurv pipeline integrating radiomics (1.2k+ features/patient) with clinical data, achieving 10% higher concordance than Cox baselines for survival prediction


Past Research
Directed Reading in Causal Inference
June 2025 - August 2025 | Rutgers University
Mentor: Dr. Nicole Pashley

Studied CBPS, AIPW/DR estimators, overlap/trim rules, and matching vs weighting methods
Built foundational understanding of causal inference methods now applied in current uncertainty quantification research


Research Assistant - Social Perception Lab
Sept 2023 - May 2024 | Rutgers University
Mentor: Dr. Lee Jussim at the Social Perception Lab

Applied Confirmatory Factor Analysis (CFA) in R to assess construct validity and model fit for psychometric scales
Contributed to refining measurement instruments used in ongoing social psychology research, improving scale reliability


Research Assistant - ABUSA REHAB Health Psychology Lab
Jan 2022 - May 2023 | Rutgers University
Mentors: Dr. Teresa Leyro at the ABUSA REHAB Lab, Dr. Samantha Farris

Conducted participant phone screens and managed data collection for smoking and stress intervention studies
Processed heart rate data using HRV/PRV software to extract physiological stress biomarkers
Data contributed to publications on stress-smoking interactions, informing behavioral intervention design


Industry Experience
Bioinformatics Data Scientist - Bristol Myers Squibb Challenge
New Brunswick, NJ

Built Proton Pulse, an interactive Streamlit tool to estimate charge variants in therapeutic proteins by integrating pI calculation and PTM site modeling
The tool enables formulation scientists to rapidly assess protein stability, reducing wet-lab iteration cycles

Live App: protonpulse.streamlit.app

Data Science Intern - IDX Exchange
New York, NY

Ingested and cleaned 2.3M MLS rows from 8 data sources; automated daily refresh with 99.5% success rate
Trained XGBoost model with geo features (schools, transit, parks), cutting RMSE by 18% and reaching MAPE 7.9% (R² 0.71 → 0.77)
Deployed home-value estimator API (p95 latency: 180ms, 99.9% uptime)
Built Tableau dashboards across 42 counties, adopted by 3 product teams, reducing ad-hoc reporting time by 60%


Quantitative Research Mentee - JPMorgan Chase & Co.
New York, NY

Engineered market-data ETL pipeline (yfinance to Parquet) with schema validation; ran 1M+ Monte Carlo stress paths, reducing VaR error by 8%
Built LSTM model for equity forecasting, improving prediction accuracy by 12%
Developed vectorized Black-Scholes pricer, increasing throughput by 15%


Teaching
Learning Assistant, Calculus II - Rutgers University
Fall 2023, Spring 2024

Led weekly problem-solving sessions for 40 students, reinforcing multivariable calculus concepts
Students showed measurable improvement in exam performance; received positive feedback on making concepts accessible


Grader, Undergraduate Statistics - Rutgers University
Fall 2024, Spring 2025, Fall 2025

Evaluated assignments and exams for 120 students across multiple semesters
Maintained consistent grading standards and provided structured feedback to help students improve


Leadership

Orientation Leader - Rutgers University: Guided 2000+ incoming students through university transition
Lead Translator - Goc Tam Ly Hoc (Vietnam): Directed a year-long initiative producing psychology education content for Vietnamese-speaking audiences
Active Member - Data Science and Quantitative Finance Clubs: Participated in collaborative projects and learning

life.title: Life & Hobbies
life.content:
Beyond statistics and neuroscience, I'm passionate about staying active, making things with my hands, and exploring the world on foot.




Running
Training for the Asbury Half Marathon and Flying Pig Marathon. Running is where I think through problems and push my limits.
Follow on Strava →









Knitting & Making
Working on sweaters and intricate patterns. A different kind of problem-solving that uses pattern-following, planning, and patience.





Coffee & Matcha
Devoted fan of specialty coffee and matcha. Always hunting for new spots in New Brunswick, Philly, and NYC.





Community
Time with friends and family makes everything worthwhile. Strength training keeps me balanced alongside long hours of desk work.









These hobbies aren't separate from my work — they're integral to it. Running clears my mind for complex problems. Knitting teaches patience. Strength training builds resilience.
